title: Weekly POC — App output hardening & SDK tuning

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Nimbus - Lead Eng), Ava Thompson (Nimbus - PM), Liam O'Rielly (Nimbus - Security)

Auto-summary: quick recap of last week's pilot telemetry, then deep-dive into three failure classes: structured output schema drift, function-calling incomplete payloads, SDK serialization/retry behavior under transient errors. Agreement to run an expanded regression and to lock candidate SDK change.

[00:00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick check, same agenda as last week — results from the sandbox run, specific failures on function call, and sdk patch walk-through.
[00:00:12] Carlos (Nimbus): yep, that's right. we had a couple of high-severity repros from staging that we want to understand.
[00:00:20] Priya (Redwood): cool. i pulled the logs you uploaded and the three top classes were: 1) structured output missing required fields; 2) function-call returned truncated args; 3) intermittent serialization errors on our python SDK when a retry happens.
[00:00:38] Ava (Nimbus): i can confirm the missing fields — our downstream consumer throws when transaction_id is absent, so that's a showstopper.
[00:00:46] Liam (Nimbus): and from a security side, any change to logging or payloads needs to be redacted; we can't see full PII in demo logs.

[00:01:15] Jordan (Redwood): good call, we'll redact. quick note — priya's already instrumented the harness to mask fields; we'll send a sanitized CSV.
[00:01:30] Priya (Redwood): yeah, i added a scrubber for account and ssn-like patterns; a few transcriptions in the logs had 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache' so we flagged those as noise too. (laughter)
[00:01:45] Carlos (Nimbus): ha, i saw that. small thing but it matter. okay so can you walk through the truncated function args case? that's the one crashing our orchestrator.

[00:02:05] Priya (Redwood): sure. in the failing runs we saw the model produce a function call payload where args were cut off at a token limit boundary — looks like the SDK's current post-processing doesn't re-check completeness for function-calling when streaming responses are enabled and a final delta arrives in a separate chunk. so we ended up with partial JSON.
[00:02:35] Jordan (Redwood): the mitigation we propose is twofold: 1) SDK-level validation that attempts to reassemble streamed deltas and validate JSON completeness before returning a function invocation; 2) a server-side fallback that retries with a short prefix to fill in missing trailing tokens. both together reduce client-visible failures.
[00:03:00] Ava (Nimbus): what about latency? retries + extra server calls could blow our SLOs.
[00:03:07] Priya (Redwood): agreed. our measurements show that for these cases the retry adds ~120-180ms on average if we do a small prefix re-query; that's within your SLO envelope for non-99.9th percentile requests. for high-percentile we'd prefer a canary route to a dedicated instance.

[00:03:35] Liam (Nimbus): ok that seems reasonable, but we need to see the histograms. can you share the p90/p99 numbers?
[00:03:42] Priya (Redwood): sure — in the sandbox run p90 increased by 0.14s and p99 by 0.6s in the worst-case with retries enabled; I'll attach the histo in the follow-up.
[00:04:00] Jordan (Redwood): moving on — the structured output drift: some prompts produce valid JSON but fields are optional, and when they are missing your consumer fails. what's your tolerance? do you want strict schema enforcement or lenient?
[00:04:18] Carlos (Nimbus): strict. our downstream reconciliation needs transaction_id, amount_cents, and currency. optional fields are ok but those three are hard requirements.
[00:04:26] Jordan (Redwood): got it. we can ship two things: SDK helper that validates schema and returns a typed error before commit, and a server-side policy that rejects responses that fail required-field checks and falls back to a simpler model variant.
[00:04:46] Ava (Nimbus): if the server rejects, do we get a clear error code? we need mapping for monitoring.
[00:04:52] Priya (Redwood): yes, we'll add a structured error code — like PROTOCOL_SCHEMA_FAIL — and surface it in the per-request diagnostics. that will appear in Console as a metric and in the token-level trace.

[00:05:12] Carlos (Nimbus): perfect. one more: the Python SDK serialization errors. we saw json.decoder errors after a retry loop. is that due to partial concatenation?
[00:05:22] Priya (Redwood): exactly. current sdk patch concatenates chunks and naively does json.loads; if a retry occurs mid-serialization there's a race where the buffer is in an inconsistent state. the fix is to hold a reassembly buffer and only call the deserializer on delineated complete payloads or to use streaming-json parsing.
[00:05:45] Jordan (Redwood): we've prepared a candidate patch for the Python and node SDKs — small change — will close the race by adding a chunk-collector + completeness check. we'll publish as 0.9.14-rc.
[00:06:00] Ava (Nimbus): can we test the rc in our staging before you flip it?
[00:06:05] Jordan (Redwood): yes, that's the plan. Priya, will you run the regression with that rc?
[00:06:10] Priya (Redwood): yep, will run with rc and with streaming on and off to cover both flows.

[00:06:38] Carlos (Nimbus): also, when the function call returns args we noticed some fields that aren't redacted — we need to ensure the logging hooks redact FSN and account numbers.
[00:06:50] Liam (Nimbus): it's critical. our compliance team won't sign off without that.
[00:06:55] Priya (Redwood): we've got the redaction layer; the current issue was we don't apply it to auxiliary trace logs. i'll make that change and re-run.

[00:07:20] Jordan (Redwood): switching to KV cache interactions — Carlos you mentioned some cache misses when you hit prefixes under 8 tokens?
[00:07:28] Carlos (Nimbus): yes, short prefixes seem to avoid the cache and we penalize for repeated similar requests. it's causing bursty qps to blow up cost.
[00:07:36] Priya (Redwood): that was a config issue on your side — the SDK default had prefix_size=8, and a number of your requests had 4-6 token prompts; we'll recommend lowering the threshold and enabling prefix bucketing. also we can enable a small adaptive cache that promotes short prefixes seen frequently.
[00:07:52] Ava (Nimbus): what's the expected cost impact?
[00:07:56] Priya (Redwood): with adaptive promotion we measured a 12-18% token cost reduction in similar workloads in our internal bench. i'll share the bench sheet.

[00:08:20] Jordan (Redwood): quick call-out on monitoring — will add a per-route metric for schema rejections, function-call truncations, and sdk-serialization failures so you can alert before consumer errors.
[00:08:35] Ava (Nimbus): great. also, would like a dashboard with the sample failing prompt and anonymized output for inspection.
[00:08:42] Priya (Redwood): we can add a sanitized example panel and a link to the exact run in Console. note: the sanitized examples will remove full acct/PII.

[00:09:05] Carlos (Nimbus): timeline — we want to go into a pre-staging run next week, then a final staging run followed by a 24h soak. are those realistic?
[00:09:14] Jordan (Redwood): yes. proposed schedule: rc SDK by Friday 2026-03-20, regression results back 2026-03-25, pre-staging 2026-03-26, final staging 2026-03-30 and 24h soak 2026-03-31.
[00:09:33] Liam (Nimbus): security review needed before final staging. i'll prepare a brief checklist and share.

[00:09:50] Priya (Redwood): on the subject of security, the KMS integration — Liam, you asked about key rotation and server-side tracing. we can use your KMS for request-level decryption and redact traces at ingest; that keeps raw payloads out of our logs.
[00:10:06] Liam (Nimbus): yes, and we need an attestation that we can disable transcript retention after 7 days.
[00:10:11] Jordan (Redwood): that's configurable per account; we'll include the config steps in the security appendix.

[00:10:35] Ava (Nimbus): small question on observability — if a schema rejection triggers a fallback to a simpler model, can we mark the event with the originating prompt id so we can reconcile?
[00:10:45] Priya (Redwood): yes, we'll populate the trace with prompt_id, request_id, and route used. we'll also emit a fallback metric so you can correlate with consumer errors.

[00:11:10] Carlos (Nimbus): are there any open questions about the SDK patch? we want the patch to be minimal, non-breaking, and fully backwards compatible.
[00:11:18] Priya (Redwood): it's additive only — we add a collector and completeness check; we don't change function call shapes. for Node and Python it's a minor API-surface bump but should be backward compatible.
[00:11:35] Jordan (Redwood): i'll drop the rc link and install notes in the chat.

[00:11:50] (silent / typing)
[00:12:12] Priya (Redwood): heads-up: i noticed two weird transcripts where the model returned 'null' for amount_cents but then included currency; that looks like a hallucination / grounding failure. would you like us to run a focused precision eval?
[00:12:30] Carlos (Nimbus): yes please — add a small eval with your auto-generated negative samples and our real prompts.

[00:12:50] Jordan (Redwood): ok, so to summarize the action items: priya runs rc regression, carlos supplies prompts, jordan shares security docs and the sdk rc, liam sends compliance checklist. anything else?
[00:13:05] Ava (Nimbus): also include instructions for running the harness locally — we had one engineer who couldn't reproduce the race locally.
[00:13:12] Priya (Redwood): will include full reproduce steps and a dockerized harness so you can run it in the same environment.

[00:13:38] (Speaker 1): question from the chat — will function-calling fallback keep conversation context?
[00:13:44] Priya (Redwood): yes, fallback preserves KV cache up to the configured TTL and the runtime will merge the prefix so context is preserved. there was a prior bug where the cache TTL wasn't honored on fallbacks; that's fixed in the rc.

[00:14:10] Carlos (Nimbus): ok good. any estimated roll-forward risk? we need to know if customer-visible change could alter outputs beyond the fix.
[00:14:19] Jordan (Redwood): the changes are narrowly scoped — reassembly and validation — so model outputs should only be different when prior behavior returned incomplete or invalid payloads. we'll run a diff to show changes.

[00:14:42] Ava (Nimbus): final ask: share a one-pager for execs summarizing risk, perf impact, and go/no-go criteria for staging.
[00:14:50] Jordan (Redwood): we'll do that.

[00:15:10] Priya (Redwood): i'll outline pass/fail thresholds: zero schema rejections in pre-staging, <0.1% function-call truncations, and no new integrity errors after SDK rc.
[00:15:28] Liam (Nimbus): acceptable. on compliance, if you can include a note on log retention and redaction, that's good.

[00:15:45] Jordan (Redwood): ok folks — quick recap of follow-ups, then we'll wrap.
[00:15:50] (Wrap-up)
[00:16:05] Jordan (Redwood): recap: 1) Priya runs full regression with 0.9.14-rc and posts results (due 3/25). 2) Carlos provides 200 prompts + repros (due 3/22). 3) Jordan posts security appendix and rc install notes (due 3/20). 4) Liam sends compliance checklist (due 3/24). 5) Schedule pre-staging 3/26 and final staging 3/30.
[00:16:38] Ava (Nimbus): thanks everyone, this was productive.
[00:16:42] Carlos (Nimbus): thanks — looking forward to the rc.
[00:16:45] Priya (Redwood): thanks, will follow up in the thread and upload sanitized logs to the shared drive.
[00:16:52] Jordan (Redwood): thanks all. meeting end.
